name: Shoreline
seo_title: 7 Christmas Events for Kids in Shoreline, WA 2026
seo_desc: 7 Christmas events for kids in Shoreline, WA, 4 free: ShoreLights Winter Light Display at the Park at Town Center and more.
lede: Shoreline does Christmas outdoors and close to home: a new winter light display next to City Hall, a neighborhood tree lighting where Santa arrives by truck, a church Santa afternoon with a petting zoo, and an evening stroll through a lit woodland garden.
celebrates: Shoreline's newest tradition is ShoreLights, a free winter light display in the Park at Town Center on Aurora Avenue North, run by Destination Shoreline with the City of Shoreline, with an opening night lighting, s'mores with the Shoreline Fire Department, food trucks and live music. In North City, Santa lights a giant tree on top of a water reservoir at the North City Tree Lighting Festival. Aurora Community Church hosts Santa Claus Lane with free pictures with Santa, a petting zoo and a snow zone. Kruckeberg Botanic Garden opens its lit woodland paths for a Winter Solstice Stroll, and the Argosy Christmas Ship visits Richmond Beach Saltwater Park.
lastyear: In 2025 Shoreline lit ShoreLights for the first time. The City of Shoreline, the Shoreline Chamber and other sponsors held the Inaugural ShoreLights Winter Lighting Ceremony on Saturday, November 15, 2025, at 5:30 pm in the Park at Town Center, with free parking at City Hall. Shoreline Area News reported the lights stayed on display through January 11, 2026. Three weeks later, on Saturday, December 6, the 26th annual North City Tree Lighting Festival brought Santa to Les Schwab on 15th Avenue NE.
facts: Shoreline is young as a city and old as a community. It incorporated in 1995, and HistoryLink notes it is now home to more than 57,000 people. Homesteaders came first, then vacationers, and by 1912 a brick road ran all the way to the county line. The old Ronald School, named for early resident Judge James Ronald, now holds the Shoreline Historical Museum. The North City tree has been lit for more than 25 years, and ShoreLights includes light sculptures of a trolley car, an arch and an orca.
trains: Railroads opened up Shoreline. The Seattle, Lake Shore and Eastern Railway reached the area in 1891, and from 1910 to 1939 the electric Interurban carried commuters between Everett and Tacoma at more than 30 miles an hour. Today Link light rail is back: Shoreline South/148th and Shoreline North/185th stations opened on the 1 Line in August 2024. For a holiday train ride, the Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie has run Santa Trains every year since 1969 on part of that same 1880s Lake Shore and Eastern line.

traditions: A free winter light display in the Park at Town Center next to Shoreline City Hall, with an opening night lighting ceremony.
Santa arrives by truck and lights a giant tree on top of North City Water District's 3.7 million gallon reservoir.
Aurora Community Church's December afternoon of free pictures with Santa, cookie decorating with Mrs. Claus, a petting zoo, a snow zone and a Christmas sing-along.
The Shoreline Fire Department roasts free s'mores over a bonfire during the ShoreLights season.
The City of Shoreline and the Richmond Beach Community Association welcome the Argosy Christmas Ship with bonfires and Santa at Richmond Beach Saltwater Park.
Kruckeberg Botanic Garden lights its woodland paths for a free evening walk near the longest night of the year.
kidfact: In North City, Santa lights a giant Christmas tree that sits on top of a water reservoir. That reservoir holds 3.7 million gallons of water.
faq: ShoreLights is Shoreline's free winter light display in the Park at Town Center, at 17550 Aurora Ave N next to City Hall. Destination Shoreline and the City of Shoreline run it, with an opening night lighting, food trucks, live music on weekend evenings and a scavenger hunt. It started in 2025 with an inaugural lighting ceremony.
Where is the North City Tree Lighting?

The festival happens at Les Schwab, 17754 15th Ave NE, near NE 180th Street. The tree itself stands on top of North City Water District's 3.7 million gallon reservoir. Santa arrives in a decorated truck the organizers call Rudolph the ReinTruck, lights the tree and stays for photos, while neighbors hand out cocoa and cookies.
Where can kids get free photos with Santa in Shoreline?

Aurora Community Church, 1900 N 175th St, hosts Santa Claus Lane each December with free pictures with Santa. The afternoon also brings cookie decorating with Mrs. Claus, a petting zoo, a snow zone, bouncy houses, crafts and giveaways, and it ends with a Christmas sing-along. Santa also appears at the North City Tree Lighting Festival.
Can we see the Argosy Christmas Ship from Shoreline?

Yes. The Christmas Ship stops at Richmond Beach Saltwater Park, 2021 NW 190th St, where the City of Shoreline and the Richmond Beach Community Association host Christmas on the Beach with bonfires and Santa. Check the city's calendar each year for the exact evening and arrival time, since the ship follows a set route along the shore.
Is there a holiday light walk in a garden near Shoreline?

Kruckeberg Botanic Garden in Shoreline holds a Winter Solstice Stroll each December, with softly lit garden paths, music and warm gathering spaces. The garden lists it as free and designed for visitors of all ages. The garden sits at 20312 15th Ave NW in the Richmond Beach neighborhood.
Can we take light rail to Shoreline's Christmas events?

Shoreline has two Link 1 Line stations, Shoreline South/148th and Shoreline North/185th, which opened in August 2024 and connect Shoreline with Seattle and Lynnwood. Community Transit buses serve Shoreline North/185th Station, and ShoreLights sits on Aurora Avenue North next to City Hall, so check a trip planner for the best bus link.

intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in Shoreline for 2026, and here is what he found: 7 family events, 4 of them free. The magic runs from December 3 (ShoreLights Winter Light Display at the Park at Town Center) through January 2, with ShoreLights Winter Light Display at the Park at Town Center (from December 3), North City Tree Lighting Festival (December 5) and Santa Claus Lane at Aurora Community Church (December 6) along the way. We check every date on the host’s own website or an official city calendar, and each listing links straight there. For the rest of the state, see our Washington Christmas events for kids guide.

Planning a bigger day out? Shoreline families also use our guide to Christmas events for kids in Seattle, which covers Seattle Center Winterfest, WildLanterns, the North Pole Limited Santa train and more.
